original_question: Given an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, which orderings {f_k}_{k in I} of its elements have the property that the ordered frame can be represented as an operator orbit {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for some bounded linear operator T? In other words, can one characterize exactly which permutations or sequential arrangements of the same Gabor frame yield a bounded generating operator?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, in its Gabor-frame specialization as motivated by Proposition 1.2 and the nearby discussion around Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's main Gabor-frame issue: start with an overcomplete lattice Gabor frame, allow a reordering of its elements, and ask whether the reordered sequence can be realized as a single bounded-operator orbit. It also correctly focuses on boundedness of the generating operator as the key difficulty.
missing_details: The paper's question is existential, not a full characterization of all admissible permutations: it asks whether there exists an appropriate ordering, not which orderings exactly work.
The ambient space should be stated explicitly as L^2(R).
The operator should be specified as a bounded linear operator T: L^2(R) -> L^2(R).
The orbit is indexed by N_0 in the paper's main formulation, i.e. {T^k phi}_{k=0}^infty, not an arbitrary index set I.
The reordered Gabor family should be described as a bijective enumeration of the frame elements.
The window and lattice parameters should be made explicit: g in L^2(R), a,b > 0, and the frame is {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}.
To be stand-alone, the modulation and translation operators should be defined: E_{mb}f(x)=e^{2 pi i mb x}f(x), T_{na}f(x)=f(x-na).
The paper does not ask for a characterization of all permutations or sequential arrangements of the same frame; that broadens the scope beyond the official formulation.

The paper's nearby context uses Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 to explain why overcomplete Gabor frames are natural candidates, so a faithful restatement should stay close to that existence question rather than adding classification language.
refined_question: Let g in L^2(R) and a,b>0 be such that the lattice Gabor system {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, where E_{mb}f(x)=e^{2 pi i mb x}f(x) and T_{na}f(x)=f(x-na), is an overcomplete frame for L^2(R). Does there exist a bijective ordering {f_k}_{k=0}^infty of the elements of this Gabor frame and a bounded linear operator T:L^2(R)->L^2(R) such that f_k=T^k f_0 for every k in N_0?
justification: The draft is closest to the paper's Gabor-frame open problem, but it overstates the scope. The paper asks an existence question about whether an overcomplete Gabor frame can, after a suitable ordering, be written as a bounded single-orbit frame. It does not ask for an exact characterization of all permutations. Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are part of the immediate context because they isolate the structural properties that motivate considering overcomplete Gabor frames as candidates for such bounded operator representations.
